rationale: Round 0 built and ran cleanly, so round 1 shifts toward stronger obfuscation while protecting the hot floating-point inner loops (Mm, rInnerproduct dominate the 849-byte text and nearly all runtime). SUB is pushed highest: arithmetic substitution is near-free in both time and size, adds real static-analysis resistance to the matrix-multiply inner products, and carries minimal correctness risk. FLA and BCF are the primary structural defenses and are kept strong, but BCF's RuntimeCost stays elevated since bogus predicates execute inside the hot matrix loops and the binary is tiny, so its size bloat is proportionally expensive. SPLIT is retained as a low-cost force multiplier whose block splitting increases the effectiveness of FLA/IBR rather than for its own sake. IBR is moderately favored to obscure the benchmark's dense branch dispatch without taxing the FP loops heavily. ICALL and IGV are held at moderate weights: with only 7 functions and few globals (matrix buffers, seed), indirect calls and hidden globals yield modest diversity but non-trivial correctness risk on pointer-heavy float/int matrix code, so they are enabled but not emphasized. Net effect: a correctness-safe baseline (SUB/SPLIT) layered with strong control-flow obfuscation (FLA/BCF) and moderate data/branch indirection, accepting bounded runtime overhead on a benchmark whose measured cost is dominated by a handful of small loops.
